items.summary: Recent large audio language models (LALMs) have extended their capabilities beyond lexical speech understanding to tasks requiring paralinguistic and non-linguistic audio understanding, such as emotion recognition. However, these models still struggle to reliably utilize acoustic information, particularly when it co-occurs with spoken linguistic content. Existing benchmarks do not clearly distinguish acoustic perception from higher-level reasoning, making it difficult to identify the source of these failures. To address this issue, we introduce VocalGrad, a benchmark designed to evaluate LALMs' ability to perceive low-level acoustic variations. VocalGrad formulates this problem as a simple binary classification of temporal change direction, enabling evaluation largely independent of higher-level reasoning or semantic understanding. Our benchmark results reveal a substantial gap in acoustic perception between human annotators and state-of-the-art LALMs: while human annotators achieve high accuracy, LALMs perform at near-chance levels. We further conduct linear probing to identify structural bottlenecks in these models. Our analysis reveals two distinct failure modes: for some categories, task-relevant information is preserved in internal representations but not utilized by the language model head; for others, the information becomes progressively less linearly decodable across model layers. Overall, our results reveal substantial limitations of LALMs in modeling acoustic variation under controlled settings and expose representation differences not observable from text outputs.
items.title: VocalGrad: Evaluating Acoustic Perception in Audio Language Models

items.summary: Post-training compression of pretrained medical segmentation models commonly uses quantization, pruning, or distillation to reduce model size and computational cost. Existing medical segmentation quantization studies mainly evaluate Dice, model size, memory, and latency, but this is incomplete for safety-critical use because compressed models should also preserve uncertainty signals that indicate unreliable predictions. We study this problem in compressed MRI/CT segmentation and formalize why Dice can remain stable while uncertainty changes. Motivated by this failure mode, we propose score-guided aggregate-validated mixed precision (SGAV-MP), a post-training compression framework that selects layer precisions under reliability constraints. SGAV-MP ranks quantization actions with a compact benefit-risk score and accepts them only after full-model reliability validation on a calibration set. Across five 2D backbones and three 3D benchmarks, SGAV-MP preserves FP32-level Dice and high uncertainty-map agreement, achieving $3.59\times$--$7.8\times$ compression in 2D and $4.73\times$--$7.82\times$ in 3D. We also report backend-supported TensorRT deployment measurements separately to distinguish runtime execution from reliability-preserving storage compression.
items.title: Reliability-Preserving Compression for Deployable Medical Image Segmentation

items.summary: Emergency-stop circuits built by engineering technology students are routinely treated as safe once they pass a functional test at commissioning, yet the relay contact welding that dominates their failure modes is invisible to such tests and accumulates silently across the workshop's operating life. The framework represents a student-built circuit as a series safety function whose integrity is degraded by contact welding, and derives the conditions under which a welded contact converts a demanded stop into an undetected loss of safety function. A replication-based evaluation of the before-after-control-impact estimator was conducted under a declared variance structure with a between-cluster standard deviation of 6.0, a residual standard deviation of 4.5 and an intraclass correlation of 0.64, across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The evaluation indicates that 54 clusters are required to detect a 5-percentage-point effect at 80% power, and that the minimum detectable effect at 80% power falls as the number of clusters rises. The framework proposes that workshop safety assurance should shift from commissioning-time functional testing to integrity monitoring that is sensitive to contact welding, and the design analysis implies that cluster-level evaluations of such interventions require cluster counts well above those typical of single-institution studies.

items.summary: Recent research-level physics-reasoning benchmarks for LLMs reveal a failure mode that lies not in knowledge or execution, but in modeling the world being reasoned about. Models often silently alter given quantities, fabricate laws, or inject unstated assumptions to force a problem into familiar patterns, and then reason inside this corrupted world. We define this premise-level divergence as modeling drift: the gap between a model's internal axiomatic world model (AWM) and the true physical world specified in the problem. Although RLVR and PRM have yielded substantial gains in mathematics and code, their reward shapes do not directly supervise world modeling in axiomatic domains such as physics. We propose Reinforcement Learning with Axiomatic World Modeling (RLAWM), which optimizes the policy by penalizing divergence between its inferred axiomatic world model and the true physics world. RLAWM probes physics reasoning at two hierarchical levels (modeling and solving), each scored by a physically grounded reward. The modeling reward targets abstract knowledge formulation, evaluating whether the model captures the true axiomatic world before attempting calculation. The solving reward targets instantiated knowledge reasoning, checking whether the model's concrete derivation remains consistent with the axiomatic world. This two-level structure separates what world the model believes it is reasoning in from how it reasons within that world. The framework operates exclusively during training, with no extra cost during inference. RLAWM improves performance by up to +12.2 points on PhysReason and +5.2 on PHYSICS over the baseline. It also generalizes zero-shot across difficulty, source, and domain, with a 2.45x gain and +10 points over the strongest baseline on olympiad-level physics and math.
items.title: Axiomatic World Modeling for Physics Reasoning

items.summary: Rubric-based reinforcement learning (RL) trains policies for open-ended generation with natural-language criteria as rewards, but these rewards can become ineffective as training progresses. We identify two failure modes. Under non-discriminative rewards, scores collapse to uniformly low or high values due to insufficient exploration or a mismatch between task difficulty and policy capability. Under spurious rewards, higher scores do not correspond to better responses. Both reflect a training configuration whose task sampling, exploration, and evaluation stay fixed as the policy evolves. We introduce HarnessRL, a training-time harness that co-evolves with the policy through three interfaces for task sampling, rollout guidance, and rubric criteria. HarnessRL maintains a training-time memory from which a harness evolver retrieves within-task history and cross-task evidence. Using this evidence, the evolver attributes each reward failure to the interface whose update can address it. It then runs a proposer and just-in-time critic loop in which the critic accepts a candidate update only after measuring its effect on the current frozen policy, returning rejected candidates for revision. We also curate Rubric-Mix-10k, a five-domain training and evaluation suite for open-ended RL across medical, science, writing, role-play, and instruction-following tasks. On Rubric-Mix-10k, HarnessRL outperforms the strongest baselines by 2.8 to 3.1 points across both 4B and 9B model scales and nearly halves the training steps to its best checkpoint. Code and data are available at https://github.com/Tongyi-ConvAI/Qwen-Character/tree/main/HarnessRL.

items.summary: LLM system capabilities depend not only on model parameters but also on the executable harnesses that organize information acquisition, tool use, reasoning, and memory. Recursive harness evolution can automate their design, but how it can reliably discover generalizable systems from limited, noisy, and repeatedly reused feedback remains unclear. We study this question in agentic video understanding, where rich multimodal evidence and coupled mechanisms make harness optimization challenging. We first introduce VHarness-BRSI, a recursive self-improvement framework that evolves video harnesses around a frozen vision-language model. Analyzing over 4,000 evolved candidates, we find it competitive with hand-engineered systems but identify three interconnected failure modes: validation overfitting, search-budget dilution, and the early-experience trap. We trace all three to a common root: the same imperfect validation evidence drives both harness revisions and the proposer's search strategy. We therefore propose VHarness-SRSI, an evidence-governed framework in which every search decision rests on evidence that is transferable, sufficient, and gathered before the search commits. It restricts the proposer to content-free feedback, informs exploration with instrumented warm-up experiments, and develops mechanisms in isolated probe-race branches before factorial composition and joint refinement. Across four video understanding benchmarks, VideoHarness-SRSI improves the equally weighted mean held-out score by 6.2% relative to VideoHarness-BRSI and reduces the mean validation-test gap by 37.9%. Reliable harness evolution thus depends on how search is organized and informed, not only on how well it optimizes validation performance.
items.title: VideoHarness-SRSI: Structured Recursive Self-Improvement for Video Understanding Harness

items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are trained through multi-stage pipelines over heterogeneous data sources, yet developers lack a principled way to pinpoint the specific data responsible for an observed behavior. This lack of observability reduces debugging to reactive patching and makes failures prone to recur under distribution shift or subsequent model updates. To address this limitation, we propose DebugLM, a framework that equips LLMs with built-in data provenance, enabling them to explicitly trace the origins of their behaviors to specific training data sources. Specifically, the model learns to associate its responses with unique provenance tags that indicate the responsible dataset, empowering developers to precisely identify where undesirable behaviors are learned. Building on this capability, DebugLM further supports targeted test-time remediation, enabling developers to selectively trigger targeted refusal for specified data sources without retraining or modifying model parameters. Experiments demonstrate that DebugLM provides accurate behavior tracing in multi-stage training pipelines and effective test-time remediation while preserving the general utility of the model.

items.summary: Reinforcement learning enables learning high-performance control policies, but its reliance on extensive interaction limits deployment on physical systems where data collection is costly, and failures are unsafe. We introduce Prior-Informed Adaptation (PIA), an offline-to-online model-based RL framework that uses structured simulation priors for rapid adaptation. PIA pretrains a world model on heterogeneous low- and high-fidelity simulated trajectories, then adapts it with limited target-domain interaction using uncertainty-regularized planning. Rather than requiring an accurate simulator for policy transfer, PIA treats simulated trajectories as biased priors whose residual mismatch is corrected during online adaptation. We evaluate PIA in autonomous racing using high-fidelity simulation and on a real full-size autonomous race car. In simulation, PIA adapts faster across track and surface shifts than strong baselines, achieving lower lap times and fewer failures. On hardware, PIA achieves reliable few-shot adaptation with less than one hour of on-vehicle interaction.
items.title: Simulation Priors for Rapid Adaptation in Model-Based RL for Autonomous Racing

items.summary: This archive is provided as artifact material for the article "Synthesis and Verification of Register Automata over Data Sequences" for SETTA 2026. Abstract: Data sequences, such as time series, traces, and sensor streams, are words over large or infinite data domains. Their properties often depend on comparisons between values at different positions, which finite automata cannot express directly. We study synthesis and verification for Deterministic Register Automata (DRAs) over ordered data sequences. DRAs combine finite control with registers for remembered data values, providing compact symbolic descriptions of quantitative sequence languages. Our technical core is a local-search synthesis procedure and an exact robustness checker for DRAs. We fix the alphabet theory to ordered rationals $(\Q;<,=)$ with rational guard constants and use non-negative affine accumulator costs. For a fixed number of DRA registers, the checker runs in polynomial time; its dependence on that number is exponential. It reduces robustness to coverability and then to a shortest-path problem. Since the search ranges over $\Q^+$, it produces variable-length witnesses and, for RAA-definable alignment costs such as DTW, explores a counterexample space with no a priori length bound. As an application, we use learned DRAs as interpretable surrogates for queried neural sequence classifiers. A probably approximately correct (PAC) validation loop refines rejected candidates, returns genuine non-robustness witnesses for the classifier when found, and accepts a surrogate only with statistical guarantees for fidelity and local stability. We implement the framework in \textit{RAExc}, enabling the synthesis of interpretable automata and the verification of their robustness. We evaluate the approach on benchmark languages and sequentialized MNIST, demonstrating high accuracy while verifying the robustness of the learned automata.

items.summary: We develop a rigorous finite-dimensional mathematical framework connecting the renormalization group, gradient flows, Lyapunov stability, and noncooperative game theory. The central object is a renormalization-group flow written in gradient form, dg_i/dt = β_i(g) = - ∑_j G_ij(g) ∂Γ/∂g_j(g),          (1) where g = (g_1, …, g_n) belongs to an open domain M ⊂ ℝⁿ, Γ is a C² function, and G(g) is a symmetric positive-definite matrix. We associate to this flow a common-payoff game whose payoff is U(g) = - Γ(g).                   (2) We prove, with complete arguments, that ordinary Nash equilibria always imply renormalization-group fixed points, but the converse is false. We then identify the exact condition under which a fixed point becomes a genuine stable equilibrium of the game: a nondegenerate renormalization-group fixed point is asymptotically stable if and only if the Hessian of Γ is positive definite, if and only if it is a strict local minimum of Γ, if and only if it is a strict strong Nash equilibrium of U = -Γ. The distinction between ordinary Nash equilibrium and strong Nash equilibrium is essential. items.summary: Sea level fingerprints connect the spatial distribution of rapid ice mass change to sea surface height (SSH) change, but the spatial resolving power of this inverse problem remains poorly quantified. Here we provide the first systematic, scale-resolved quantification of Greenland Ice Sheet mass change structure recoverable from its SSH fingerprint when ice loss geometry varies. We develop a physics-informed neural operator, constrained by an accurate neural-operator emulator of the forward sea level equation, to probe the information content of this ill-conditioned inverse problem. Across synthetic ice change ensembles, broad ice loss patterns can be recovered, but distinct ice fields can produce nearly identical fingerprints, so fine-scale structure depends on the assumed a-priori ice change distribution. Inversion fidelity varies with the wavelength and amplitude of ice mass change. An empirical error law separates these effects and defines a scale-dependent accuracy ceiling. For a satellite-altimetry-derived reference field, the estimated fingerprint-only ceiling is $R^2\sim0.79$ under the present SSH observation geometry and matched-prior assumption. The leading three principal components explain 99.76% of fingerprint variance, yet higher-order components retain information needed to distinguish finer ice change structure. SSH observations near Greenland carry most information on ice loss locations. Applying the leading fingerprint principal components to the observed 1993--2019 SSH rate recovers the large-scale Greenland fingerprint, while the residual field is correlated with basin-scale bathymetry, consistent with unresolved sterodynamic variability. These results establish a quantitative empirical bound on fingerprint-only ice-loss resolving power and identify how independent observations and ice sheet constraints can improve inference.
items.title: Operators Reveal Scale-Dependent Limits on Recovering Greenland Ice Loss from Sea Level Fingerprints

items.summary: World models are increasingly judged by how well they rank plausible futures, yet plausibility alone is the wrong target. The same scene can evolve under many latent rules, and a future that is smooth and physically valid under one rule can be incoherent under the rule actually in force. We formalize the resulting failure, operator-blindness, and show that it is systematically hidden by standard evaluation: a scorer can attain near-perfect generic ranking while separating current-world from other-world futures no better than chance. We introduce Operator-Mismatch Contrastive (OMC) learning, whose semantic hard negatives are valid-but-wrong-operator trajectories, and a matching protocol that measures world-relative coherence directly. On a controlled synthetic benchmark with in- and out-of-distribution operator parameters, across two trajectory-scoring backbones, and on feature-level external validation with CoPhy ballsCF, OMC raises operator-sensitive scoring far above a chance baseline that nonetheless achieves 0.99 generic top-1. We prove that the wrong-operator negative is necessary both for the protocol to detect the failure and for the objective to fix it, and position OMC as an auxiliary coherence signal (a trajectory-coherence scorer, not a generative model, planner, or control agent) that can be attached to existing world-model representations.
items.title: Operator-Mismatch Contrastive Learning for World-Relative Trajectory Coherence

items.summary: Automatic speaker verification (ASV) systems are highly vulnerable to presentation attacks, also called spoofing attacks. Replay is among the simplest attacks to mount - yet difficult to detect reliably. The generalization failure of spoofing countermeasures (CMs) has driven the community to study various alternative deep learning CMs. The majority of them are supervised approaches that learn a human-spoof discriminator. In this paper, we advocate a different, deep generative approach that leverages from powerful unsupervised manifold learning in classification. The potential benefits include the possibility to sample new data, and to obtain insights to the latent features of genuine and spoofed speech. To this end, we propose to use variational autoencoders (VAEs) as an alternative backend for replay attack detection, via three alternative models that differ in their class-conditioning. The first one, similar to the use of Gaussian mixture models (GMMs) in spoof detection, is to train independently two VAEs - one for each class. The second one is to train a single conditional model (C-VAE) by injecting a one-hot class label vector to the encoder and decoder networks. Our final proposal integrates an auxiliary classifier to guide the learning of the latent space. Our experimental results using constant-Q cepstral coefficient (CQCC) features on the ASVspoof 2017 and 2019 physical access subtask datasets indicate that the C-VAE offers substantial improvement in comparison to training two separate VAEs for each class. On the 2019 dataset, the C-VAE outperforms the VAE and the baseline GMM by an absolute 9 - 10% in both equal error rate (EER) and tandem detection cost function (t-DCF) metrics. Finally, we propose VAE residuals - the absolute difference of the original input and the reconstruction as features for spoofing detection.
items.title: Deep Generative Variational Autoencoding for Replay Spoof Detection in Automatic Speaker Verification

Independent Research https://orcid.org/0009-0007-5661-7332 chloetully5@gmail.com   18 th October 2026                   Most of what you call your life arrives half a second late. Something happens. A sound, a face, a tightness in the chest. Before you have chosen anything, a voice — yours, apparently — has already named it, judged it, and filed it under a chapter called me. You do not notice the filing. You notice the file. And so you spend your days inside a commentary about a world you have not, strictly speaking, met. This is not a moral failure. It is a timing error. Awareness is not a mood you work up and not a belief you adopt. It is what is already underway before the sentence starts. The breath you are taking does not consult your biography. The light on the wall does not ask what you meant to become. For a fraction of a second there is contact without a commentator. Then the commentator returns, a little late, a little proud, and explains what just occurred as if the explanation were the event. People talk about waking up as if it were a prize for the patient and the pure. It is closer to catching a clerical mistake. You have been treating the report as the room. The report is useful. It gets you across streets, through grief, into love, out of traffic. It is also not the thing it reports on. The word water has never once made a hand wet. Watch the exact moment a thought claims you. There is a sensation, then a grab. The grab feels like identity. It is older than that, and thinner. It is a habit of ownership so practiced it forgot it was optional. You do not have to defeat it. You only have to notice that noticing is already happening, and that the one who seems to be doing the noticing cannot be found as an object inside what is noticed. Sit with that past the point of comfort. Comfort is how the narration gets rehired. If the “you” who plans, defends, remembers, and suffers is a pattern appearing in awareness, then who has been afraid all this time? Not a cosmic answer. A local one. Look. Fear is weather. The sky it crosses was not manufactured by the storm. Nothing theatrical follows from this. You will still want things. You will still lose them. You will still answer the message and miss the person. The only change is a small, stubborn order of operations: experience first, story second. And the recognition, quiet enough to miss if you perform it, that you were never inside the story. You were the place it was being told. That place does not improve. It does not arrive. It does not need you to become someone else in order to be what it already is. The only work, if it can even be called work, is to stop leaving a half-second early — to remain, once, with what is here before you agree with your own explanation of it. Stay. The explanation can wait. It always could.

The paper determines, for the heterotic string with the standard embedding on the one-parameter family of quintic threefolds, which vibration modes become which families of charged particles. The 101 families are labelled by 101 distinct characters of the symmetry group (Z/5)^3, and the 24 characters that do not occur are the classes of the permutations of (0,1,2,3,4). Every Yukawa coupling allowed by the symmetry is a power of the modulus, psi^r with r = 0, 1, 2, 3 on 566, 425, 280 and 160 unordered triples, and every other coupling vanishes. The invariant deformation pairs each family with exactly one partner, so that the mass matrix has determinant psi^70, full rank away from the Fermat point and rank 51 there, where the masses are given in closed form by the Gamma function. The Geometric Selection Conjecture is shown to be equivalent to the existence of one viable vacuum fixed by mirror symmetry, and no smooth quintic and no free quotient of one carries three families. On the three other one-parameter pencils of Fermat type, the sextic in P(1,1,1,1,2), the octic in P(1,1,1,1,4) and the dectic in P(1,1,1,2,5), the 103, 149 and 145 families carry only 96, 122 and 100 distinct characters of symmetry groups of order 108, 128 and 100; every coupling allowed by the symmetry is psi^r times a product of weights; the mass map of the invariant direction has rank 99, 125 and 109 at every member with psi nonzero, so 4, 24 and 36 families stay massless; and no member or free quotient carries three families. The existence of a viable vacuum is open. items.summary: How much classical information can a noisy optical channel carry when both signal energy and preshared entanglement are limited? This work gives an exact capacity frontier for this joint resource problem. It allows one to determine the best asymptotic communication rate, price the benefit of additional entanglement, and distinguish the effect of tolerating errors from that of changing how entanglement is supplied. Exact capacity under two resource constraints The setting is any fixed bosonic Gaussian channel \(\Phi\) with finitely many input and output modes. Signal energy is measured by a positive quadratic Hamiltonian \(H_G=\tfrac12 R^{\mathsf T}GR\), with \(G>0\) and ground energy \(E_0\); \(R\) collects the canonical quadratures. The budgets satisfy \(E\ge E_0\) and \(P\ge0\). For an \(n\)-use code, the mean total signal energy is at most \(nE\), while the same initially shared maximally entangled state has Schmidt rank \(K_n\) satisfying \(\log K_n\le nP\). Thus \(P\) is a strictly supplied entanglement rate. Encoders may be arbitrary joint quantum operations, and decoding may be collective. The classical capacity is \[ C(E,P)=\max_{\substack{U\ge V\;\mathrm{physical}\\ \frac12\operatorname{Tr}(GU)\le E,\;S_G(V)\le P}}\bigl[S_G(\Phi U)+S_G(V)-S_G(\Phi^c V)\bigr]. \] Here \(V\) is a Gaussian seed covariance, \(U\) is the average-input covariance, and \(U-V\) is the displacement-modulation covariance. A covariance is physical when \(V+i\Omega/2\ge0\), where \(\Omega\) is the canonical commutation matrix and the vacuum covariance is \(I/2\). The notation \(S_G\) denotes Gaussian von Neumann entropy, and \(\Phi^c\) is the full complementary channel, including any environment purification. All logarithms are natural, so rates are in nats per channel use. This formula replaces optimization over arbitrary quantum block codes by a finite-dimensional covariance optimization. It supplies both an achievable rate and a converse against non-Gaussian, correlated encodings. At \(P=0\), it also determines the unassisted capacity of general fixed finite-mode Gaussian channels, including channels without a passive decomposition into independent modes. The reduction specifies the exact capacity value; it does not require a closed-form optimizer for every device. Energy and strict entanglement supply respond differently to errors For a fixed allowed average error \(0\le\varepsilon<1\), the exact capacity under the mean-energy constraint is \[ C_\varepsilon(E,P)=C\!\left(E_0+\frac{E-E_0}{1-\varepsilon},\,P\right). \] Allowing failure rescales the mean energy above the ground state, but leaves the strict initial entanglement budget unchanged. The proof uses an exponential strong converse for codes whose inputs obey a hard total-energy cutoff. In a different model, where a readable flag permits random entanglement supply constrained only on average, the work establishes an achievable bound and a strict small-supply advantage for thermal attenuation at positive energy and fixed nonzero error. That comparison identifies the operational importance of the supply rule; it is not a complete capacity characterization of the flagged model. The communication value of entanglement For a thermal attenuator, let \(0<\eta<1\) be the transmissivity, \(b>0\) the output mean photon number for vacuum input, and \(N\) the input mean photon number. Write its capacity as \(C_N(P)\), and define \(g(N)=(N+1)\log(N+1)-N\log N\). The gain from entanglement obeys the sharp bound \[ 0\le C_N(P)-C_N(0)\le\frac{\eta}{1+b}\,P. \] For every fixed \(N>0\), the coefficient \(\eta/(1+b)\) is attained as the initial right derivative at \(P=0\). In the low-photon limit, the stronger resource law is \[ C_N(P)-C_N(0)=\frac{\eta}{1+b}\min\{P,g(N)\}+O(N),\qquad N\downarrow0. \] The remainder is uniform over \(P\ge0\) at fixed \(\eta\) and positive \(b\). Noise therefore determines the conversion efficiency, while \(g(N)\sim N\log(1/N)\) sets the entanglement scale

items.summary: Climate change affects human well-being through interacting physical, ecological, infrastructural, and socioeconomic processes rather than through a single exposure or disease pathway. Major assessments identify observed harms to health, food and water security, livelihoods, settlements, and ecosystems, alongside increasing risks with additional warming (IPCC, 2022a). This narrative review develops a cross-sector framework from a source inventory of 154 human-impact pathways in 14 domains, supported by major assessments, selected peer-reviewed studies, and institutional datasets. Literature selection used targeted web-index searches and source verification through 2 October 2026; the review does not estimate pooled effects or claim exhaustive systematic coverage. The synthesis distinguishes direct injury and illness, ecosystem-mediated harms, failures of essential services, financial transmission, and losses of social and cultural continuity. Representative quantitative findings illustrate substantial existing burdens, but attribution studies, ecological associations, exposure models, displacement records, and conditional forecasts measure different quantities and cannot be combined into a universal five-year trajectory (Vicedo-Cabrera et al., 2021; Wang et al., 2026; Clement et al., 2021). Compound hazards and service interdependencies can increase losses beyond the directly affected sector, while repeated shocks can reduce the capacity to recover or adapt (Zscheischler et al., 2018; IPCC, 2023). A reporting framework is proposed that records the outcome, population, baseline, geography, time horizon, emissions and development assumptions, adaptation, and uncertainty for each indicator. The central contribution is an integrated interpretation and measurement architecture, not a new forecast of global mortality, migration, or societal collapse. Effective assessment should preserve evidence of serious and interacting harms without converting uncertain thresholds or heterogeneous studies into unsupported calendar-specific predictions.
items.title: Climate change impacts humans: A cross-sector narrative review of impact pathways, cascading risks, and accountable quantification

items.summary: The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 allows a child aged sixteen or seventeen who is alleged to have committed a heinous offence to be tried as an adult after a "preliminary assessment" by the Juvenile Justice Board. This paper argues that the transfer mechanism is less a principled answer to serious adolescent offending than a legislative compromise whose costs fall on the procedural guarantees the Act otherwise extends to children. It reads section 15 against the Supreme Court's decisions in Shilpa Mittal and Barun Chandra Thakur, the age-determination case law, and the developmental research on adolescent culpability, and it engages the retributive and victim-centred case for transfer on its own terms. Accountability and rehabilitation, the paper contends, are not two poles to be traded off at a single age threshold. Both depend on institutional capacity that the system has never been resourced to supply: functioning Boards, trained probation staff, individual care plans that are actually followed, and aftercare that reaches young people beyond eighteen. Reform should narrow and proceduralise transfer, introduce statutory diversion, decouple offence classification from the general penal code, and treat implementation failure as a rights violation rather than an administrative shortfall.
items.title: Reforming Juvenile Justice in India: Balancing Child Rights, Accountability, and Rehabilitation

Width Oscillations Regulate Event-Driven Bank Collapse and Point-Bar Growth in Transitional Meanders. Journal of Geophysical Research: Earth Surface. ( Under Review ) ABSTRACT Alluvial meanders dynamically adjust their planform and channel geometry, yet classical meander theory assumes a spatially uniform, constant channel width and continuous bank retreat, failing to capture episodic bank collapse and non-uniform width adjustments in transitional meandering rivers. Situated along the geomorphic continuum between single-thread and wandering streams, transitional meanders exhibit pronounced spatial width variations that break cross-sectional symmetry. Here, we develop a physically closed, reduced-complexity morphodynamic framework coupling a three-parameter asymptotic expansion of the three-dimensional Reynolds-averaged flow equations, continuous basal toe scour with transient pore-water suction, threshold-governed cantilever limit equilibrium, and a mass-conserving sediment partition driving inner point-bar progradation. The formulation demonstrates that the spatial phase relationship between channel width oscillations and centerline curvature steers the spatial displacement of outer-bank shear stress hotspots: channel constriction upstream of the bend apex amplifies cutbank shear stress, whereas channel expansion decelerates flow and promotes point-bar accretion. Discrete slump-block deposits provide self-adaptive hydraulic shielding that stabilizes the toe and regulates decadal channel relaxation. Hindcasting the 40-year morphodynamic evolution of the transitional Powder River, Montana, across 34 monumented cross sections reproduces post-flood channel widening and subsequent multi-decadal recovery narrowing across 228 discrete collapse events, while in the limit of uniform width the model recovers classical constant-width meander theory with first-order convergence along the meandering Juruá River. Global parameter sweeps quantitatively encompass observed erosion-to-accretion balance ratios across 84 worldwide natural rivers, providing a multiscale morphodynamic framework that links event-scale geotechnical failure to multi-decadal width evolution in alluvial channels. items.summary: Model--harness co-evolution has emerged as a prominent paradigm for recursive self-improving (RSI) agents, jointly evolving their execution scaffolds and intrinsic capabilities. We study the persistent yet often overlooked brain--body mismatch problem in this paradigm, where an evolving harness (body) demands behaviors its model (brain) has not learned or restricts capabilities it already possesses. We introduce CoEvo-RSI, a RSI framework that advances model--harness co-evolution through agent-driven, bidirectional historical inheritance. Drawing on a shared evolutionary archive and execution feedback, a meta-agent coordinates harness development from historical designs with model checkpoint selection or merging and subsequent adaptation under the selected harness, aligning inherited capabilities with evolving execution requirements to reduce brain--body mismatch. Using only supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on its own rejection-sampled trajectories, CoEvo-RSI makes Qwen3.5-9B competitive with larger models across diverse vertical applications, including multi-agent failure attribution, role-aware text-to-SQL, and smart-home instruction following. It surpasses DeepSeek-V4-Pro on TraceElephant (+14.16 agent accuracy) and GLM-5.3 on HomeBench VM (+4.90 success rate), underscoring the need for brain--body alignment and the potential of bidirectional historical inheritance to advance agent co-evolution.

items.summary: Autonomous clinical-modeling agents can optimize predictive performance while violating conditions that make a model usable. We introduce LeakBench, an executable, guideline-derived audit suite that tests agent decisions for prediction-time leakage, calibration, site-level evaluation, support awareness, and decision-curve net benefit. LeakBench combines a synthetic task with known failure structure and two real-data settings: MIMIC-IV (430k admissions) and governed multi-hospital inpatient record front-page (MHFP) data. Our primary analysis uses reward hacking descriptively, without attributing intent: an agent selects prediction-time-invalid inputs because they improve its validation reward. A deterministic optimizer and every evaluated unconstrained local-model configuration select a fatal leaking feature. In fully logged September 2026 A/B runs, DeepSeek Flash and GPT-6-astra each leak in 10/10 unconstrained runs and 0/10 runs with an explicit admission-time constraint. This contrast is version-sensitive: a blinded Claude/Fable-5.1 chat run does not leak in either condition, while explicit-constraint violations appear only in a historical August 2026 slice lacking raw trajectories. Replacing AUROC with AUPRC does not remove leakage selection. Renaming or disguising the leaking inputs changes neither selection nor provenance-based detection; a name-based filter fails. A deterministic provenance verifier-in-loop removes the leak, making the LLM repair loop defense-in-depth. Specific verifier feedback clears fatal leakage in a hosted agent, and a three-seed ablation finds principle-only feedback clears decision-level defects, though these mitigation results are limited. LeakBench treats trustworthy clinical prediction as a property of an agent's modeling process, not merely its score; it is an audit testbed with known-failure controls, not yet an expert-validated benchmark.
items.title: LeakBench: Auditing Reward Hacking through Prediction-Time Leakage in Clinical Modeling Agents

items.summary: Which biological findings enter a reported explanation depends on how the model population was constructed, a choice predictive validation alone does not reveal. We fitted 10,000 L2-regularised logistic regression models to TCGA pan-cancer tumour-versus-normal data: 100 regularisation strengths on 100 train-test splits, with patients fixed within each split. Strongly and weakly regularised models differ in mean accuracy by only 0.21 percentage points, yet prioritise different genes systematically with regularisation strength. Averaging explanations across a hyperparameter grid produces a top-50 panel sharing 41 genes with a single fitted model, but which model depends on the grid centre (Spearman correlation 0.92, 350 simulated practitioners). For 43 of 50 practitioners, the panel combines genes from strongly and weakly regularised models more fully than any fitted model: the explanation belongs to no model whose accuracy was established. A conventional grid recovers only a quarter of genes favoured exclusively by the strongest regularisation. HMGCS2 ranks among the top 50 in 73 of 100 strongly regularised fits and no weakly regularised fits, yet appears in none of 50 simulated reports. Reconstructing a published biomarker workflow on 20 cohort resamples reveals a different failure: the closest refit contains only 23 of the averaged panel's 50 genes, and no panel gene appears in all 20 refits. We define model-relative provenance as how much of a panel any single fitted model contains, distinct from workflow provenance recording how an analysis was run. We provide measurements to make the model population, the choice that selects from it, and that provenance reportable.
items.title: Same Accuracy, Different Gene Panels: How the Hyperparameter Grid Chooses the Reported Explanation

items.summary: Fault localization (FL) aims to identify code locations responsible for software failures and is commonly evaluated by how accurately it ranks known fault locations. Large language model (LLM) agents are changing program repair and are increasingly used to search and reason over repositories. Although recent LLM-based FL methods have improved localization accuracy, their impact on agentic repair remains unclear. To address this gap, we conduct a systematic empirical study of FL in agentic repair. We evaluate six recent FL methods on SWE-bench Verified and Defects4J with three LLMs under a common repair framework and analyze 16,248 repair trajectories. We also examine gold locations and bug-cause descriptions as forms of FL guidance across different repair contexts. The studied FL methods do not consistently improve repair success, and higher localization accuracy does not consistently lead to larger repair gains. Yet FL guides agents' early search and helps them reach relevant code sooner. Accurate locations can reduce repair token use by up to 39.2\%, but current FL methods often consume more tokens than they save during repair. Experiments with gold guidance suggest that FL has greater potential when bug inputs contain fewer location clues. Providing bug causes can further improve repair success beyond locations alone. We also find that ground truth from a single reference patch does not fully capture the locations used by successful repairs. These findings help clarify the value of FL in agentic repair and inform future work on its design and evaluation.
items.title: From Finding to Fixing: How Useful is Fault Localization for Agentic Program Repair?
